facts.value: Begins the grabbing fighter CatchCut reaction by assigning situation-dependent velocity from facing direction and common-data fields, entering CatchCut, and optionally invoking the linked victim CaptureCut entry. Exact movement direction depends on the external tuning values.
facts.rationale: Narrow sign-dependent recoil or unconditional actionability claims to verified formulas and dispatcher behavior.

evidence.why: Release helper clears captor-side victim link.

facts.value: If ground_or_air equals GA_Air, writes self_vel.x = -facing_dir*x374 and self_vel.y = x378. Otherwise writes gr_vel = -facing_dir*x370. Then enters ftCo_MS_CatchCut with flags0, frame0, speed1, blend0 and NULL alternate source. A true second argument calls CaptureCut_Enter on victim_gobj after the motion change; false skips that call. No null-victim guard is present.
facts.rationale: Narrow sign-dependent recoil or unconditional actionability claims to verified formulas and dispatcher behavior.

evidence.why: Release helper clears captor-side victim link.

facts.value: Supplies the animation-expiry boundary of the captor CatchCut reaction. Once frames are exhausted it invokes the common completion dispatcher: airborne fighters enter Fall; others use a dispatcher that includes special grounded branches and ordinary Wait. Immediate actionability is not guaranteed by this callback alone.
facts.rationale: Narrow sign-dependent recoil or unconditional actionability claims to verified formulas and dispatcher behavior.

evidence.why: Air completion falls; other situations use common dispatcher.
Ground dispatcher has special branches before ordinary Wait.

facts.value: Eight-byte small-data constant pool containing consecutive float zero and one at source-object symbols @93 and @94, offsets 0 and 4. The source object marks .sdata2 WRITE|ALLOC (ELF flags 3); the original split object marks the same eight-byte payload ALLOC (flags 2). The values parameterize the CatchCut motion transition.
facts.rationale: Both existing objects and the frozen report corroborate the eight-byte payload. Object-specific flags differ, so no blanket nonwritable claim is made.

evidence.why: Zero frame/blend and unit speed arguments.

facts.value: Defines the captor-side CatchCut release lifecycle: situation-specific entry velocity and optional victim release, animation completion dispatch, an empty IASA phase, grounded traction or aerial physics, and situation-dependent terrain collision handling.
facts.rationale: Full owned source and complementary CaptureCut entry establish unit responsibilities.

evidence.why: Entry, animation, no-op IASA, physics and collision lifecycle.
